experience.cue: The agent writes rows through a parameterized SQL tool, and the harness gives the binding rules only in prose ("use $n placeholders, never inline literals", "set the timestamp to now()"). Early tool calls fail on type mismatches, params sent as a string, or a server-side timestamp bound as a parameter.
experience.lesson: In system_prompt, give one literal, copyable write statement per table. Put the casts on non-text placeholders in the SQL (`$3::boolean`, `$6::int`), write server-computed columns as functions in the SQL text (`handled_at = now()`, never a param), and add one example params JSON array in placeholder order. Separately, change the tool_hints entry for "no parameter $n" so it says params must be a JSON array, not a quoted string.
experience.evidence: Template row. inv1, agg1 and agg2 had the template, and each first UPDATE succeeded with zero errors. base1, base2, dom1, dom2 and inv2 had prose only, and each lost 2–5 retries on the first UPDATE. handled_at row: all six candidates used now() from the first write, while both base runs bound created_at. tool_hints row: under the revised hint, agg1 L227→L233 and inv2 L151→L157 fixed a string-params call in one retry; dom1 and dom2 repeated the mistake 2–3 times under the old hint.
